DS-UNIVERSAL.statement: For both Weil-manuscript families, every rational Hodge class on every self-power is supplied by full cohomology of CM abelian varieties through rational algebraic correspondences and has a rational Hodge lift. Algebraicity additionally requires the separate CM Hodge theorem.

DS-SPANNING.statement: The all-degree classical invariant spanning theorems and simultaneous projection onto balanced generator lines work for one fixed CM-line list, including dependent spanning lines and arbitrary repetitions.

DS-PADDING.statement: Actual positive CM elliptic polarizations pad every smaller quadratic determinant with signature entries at most three to a hyperbolic Weil sixfold; Markman's Weil plane and nonzero algebraic contractions supply the original determinant.

DS-BALANCE.statement: All configurations in the reviewed actual-column covering list for the two families satisfy determinant-supply condition (d), by integral opposite cancellation and diagonal integer kernels for the exceptional higher-center cases.

AG-UNIVERSAL.statement: For every complex abelian variety A of dimension at most six with a unital imaginary-quadratic action, the actual derived Hodge-group images on non-CM Albert columns are the full independent classical groups in the manuscript's small-column list, after admissible matrix-copy identifications and pairing opposite CM embeddings. This verifies condition (c), not determinant supply, central-character independence, or the Hodge conjecture.

AG-FOUNDATIONS.statement: For the actual polarized weight-one Hodge structure of a simple abelian factor, the rational Hodge group is connected reductive, its commutant is the full opposite endomorphism division algebra, and Albert columns have the divisibilities, multiplicities and polarization-pairing signs used in the small-column reduction.

AG-WEIGHTS.statement: Hodge-circle minimality and the two weights +1,-1 imply that every nontrivial simple-ideal constituent of every actual Albert column is minuscule, including constituents at pure embeddings after scalar transport.

AG-COLUMNS.statement: The dimension-six budget and a unital imaginary-quadratic action force exactly the manuscript's necessary list of non-CM column projections; this is a covering list, not an assertion that every numerical tuple is realized by an abelian variety.

AG-DESCENT.statement: A derived intertwiner between columns mixed in every scalar conjugate, with standard modules identified up to derived duality, has zero Hodge-circle shift in every conjugate and descends coefficientwise to the full rational Hodge commutant. It cannot join distinct isogeny factors or distinct nonopposite center embeddings.

AG-LINKS.statement: All proper semisimple subdirect graph links among the permitted actual column projections are impossible: ordinary links contradict the full commutant; partially pure prime-sized Galois orbits and the two SO4 ideals exclude their internal and external links; SO6/SL4 unequal modules cannot coexist within dimension six.

AG-ALGEBRA.statement: Exact root-system enumeration through the provably sufficient rank bound, rational invariant-form/commutant calculations, and exhaustive dimension-six parameter and graph-partition enumeration certify the algebraic case reduction. The computation alone makes no assertion of geometric realizability or of a formal proof of the analytic Hodge-theoretic bridge.

ks10:main:generic.statement: Assume Hg(V)=SO(V,q). The following are equivalent: (i) some complex abelian B and α∈CH²(S×B)_Q induce a nonzero map α_*:V→H²(B,Q); (ii) some smooth connected projective surface Y admits a dominant generically finite morphism f:Y→S for which the trace f_* of the image of Λ²H⁰(Y,Ω¹_Y)→H⁰(Y,Ω²_Y) is nonzero; (iii) for any stipulated standard data on T, a cycle Γ_S exactly realizes κ_S as in eq:cycle-target. In this situation T=V. The same input realizes the standard full primitive Clifford construction with the cup form.

ks10:main:specialization.statement: Fix a component of the moduli space of primitively amply polarized K3 surfaces of degree 2d. If condition (i) or (ii) of main:generic holds very generally in that component, then every (S,h) in it has the exact prescribed cycle Γ_S for every stipulated standard datum on T(S). It suffices that, about each desired point, the input holds outside countably many proper closed analytic subsets of a full polarized period chart; an algebraically very-general input suffices. Witness cycles, abelian varieties, and covers need not vary in a family.

ks10:main:all-degrees.statement: If the hypothesis of main:specialization holds in the required polarized components in every degree, then every projective K3 surface has a cycle realizing its prescribed κ_S.

ks10:cyc:h1.statement: For complex abelian varieties P,Q, pullback identifies Hom(Q,P)⊗Q with Hom_HS(H¹(P,Q),H¹(Q,Q)). Arbitrary rational weight-one Hodge maps therefore act algebraically and independently on the two slots of an ordered tensor product of first cohomologies; they need not preserve chosen polarizations.

ks10:cyc:projectors.statement: Every cohomological Künneth projector on a product of abelian varieties is induced by a rational algebraic correspondence. For U=H¹(B,Q), the mixed part of pullback along addition B×B→B injects H²(B,Q)=Λ²U into U⊗U by u∧v↦u⊗v−v⊗u.

ks10:cyc:descent.statement: Let E be a finite-dimensional rational vector space of cohomological maps and E_alg its subspace of actions of rational algebraic correspondences of a fixed degree. For every field extension K/Q, E∩(E_alg⊗K)=E_alg inside E⊗K. The assertion remains true after restricting actions to a specified rational source subspace.

ks10:cyc:equivalence.statement: Under the full-Hodge-group setting of main:generic, its nonzero correspondence condition (i) and surface-cover wedge-trace condition (ii) are equivalent. The implication from (ii) to a nonzero correspondence on V does not require the full Hodge-group hypothesis; the converse uses injectivity on V.

ks10:cliff:construction.statement: For H,Q and the sign/orientation conventions of context:clifford, P_H^± are polarizable weight-one Hodge structures; m^Q:H(1)→Hom(P_H^+,P_H^-), x↦L_x, is a rational Hodge embedding. Right multiplication by any fixed invertible odd Clifford element gives a rational Hodge isomorphism of the parity spaces. On a sufficiently small period chart their filtrations vary holomorphically and admit fixed rational polarizations.

ks10:cliff:slots.statement: If f:H(1)→Hom(P,M) is algebraically realized and a:M→M', b:P'→P are rational weight-one Hodge maps, then x↦a f(x)b is algebraically realized. This remains true under changing chosen duality isomorphisms, interchanging tensor factors with the appropriate Künneth sign, and rational Hodge identifications with isogenous abelian models.

ks10:gen:genericity.statement: In every sufficiently small full-dimensional marked polarized period chart, Hg(V)=SO(V,q) holds outside a countable union of proper closed analytic subsets. At every such point V is irreducible as a rational Hodge structure and T(S)=V.

ks10:gen:joint-group.statement: Assume Hg(V)=SO(V,q), let B be any complex abelian variety, U=H¹(B,Q), W^±=C^±(V,q), and let h be the Lie algebra of their joint Hodge group with V. Then h=g⊕k as commuting rational ideals, g≅so(V,q), and k is the kernel on V. The ideal k acts trivially on both W^±, and g acts there by the usual left spin action.

ks10:gen:width.statement: In the joint-group setting, U_C=(Δ⊗M)⊕M₀ and W_C^±=Δ⊗N_± as g_C-modules, where M₀ is trivial and dim N_±=2¹⁰. Every rational g-equivariant map U→W^± is a weight-one Hodge map, and Hom_HS(U,W^±)⊗C=Hom_g_C(U_C,W_C^±)≅Hom_C(M,N_±).

ks10:gen:vector-multiplicity.statement: For the vector module V_C of so₂₁(C) and its spin module Δ, Hom_g_C(V_C,Δ⊗Δ) has dimension one. Neither Δ nor the trivial representation contains a copy of V_C.

ks10:gen:generation.statement: Assume Hg(V)=SO(V,q), and suppose some α∈CH²(S×B)_Q induces a nonzero V→H²(B,Q). For every ε₁,ε₂∈{+,-}, every abelian realization H¹(A_j,Q)=W^{ε_j}, and every rational Hodge map β:V→W^{ε₁}⊗W^{ε₂}⊂H²(A₁×A₂,Q), there exists Γ∈CH²(S×A₁×A₂)_Q whose action restricted to V is β. In particular the full primitive Clifford multiplication tensor and its prescribed even-Clifford realization are recovered.

ks10:spec:hilbert-map.statement: Let p:X→D be a smooth proper holomorphic family of nonempty pure n-dimensional varieties over a connected complex manifold, equipped with a relative embedding X⊂D×P^N. Then there are a reduced complex quasi-projective scheme H, a smooth projective algebraic family U→H, and a holomorphic η:D→H^an such that X is its embedded analytic pullback.

ks10:spec:flat-cycle.statement: Let f:M→R be a smooth projective algebraic family of relative dimension n over a smooth irreducible complex variety R of dimension b. If Z⊂M is flat over R with fibers of dimension n−2, then r↦cl([Z_r]_{n−2}) in H⁴(M_r,Q) is a section of R⁴f_*^an Q. The notation [Z_r]_{n−2} uses generic scheme lengths and ignores smaller-dimensional components; the claim includes nonpure and nonreduced fibers.

ks10:spec:specialization.statement: Let D be a connected polydisc and p:X→D a smooth proper holomorphic family of n-dimensional varieties, n≥2, with a relative embedding in D×P^N. For a flat rational θ∈H⁰(D,R⁴p_*Q), if θ_t is the class of a rational codimension-two algebraic cycle for very general t, then it is such a class for every t∈D.

ks10:spec:local.statement: For any primitively amply polarized (S₀,h), after shrinking a full-dimensional polarized period polydisc D about its period, there exist smooth proper holomorphic K3 and abelian families S→D and A→D. The K3 family has central fiber (S₀,h), relative ample line bundle and integral H² marking; its primitive rational local system is the fixed rank-21 (V,q). The abelian family's marked H¹ is the full W=C⁺(V,q). Fixed rational polarization and parity data give flat standard tensors μ_t:V→H¹(A_t)⊗H¹(A_t). After shrinking, S×_D A×_D A embeds relatively in D×P^N.

ks10:spec:primitive.statement: Fix a polarized moduli component. If the nonzero algebraic input of main:generic holds very generally, then at every (S₀,h) in that component the standard full primitive Clifford tensor is induced by a rational codimension-two cycle. The same holds for an input outside countably many proper closed analytic subsets of a full polarized chart about each desired point.

ks10:data:restriction.statement: At any polarized K3 fiber, with q₀=q|_T, algebraic realization of primitive Clifford multiplication m^q on V implies algebraic realization of m^{q₀} on T. No full-Hodge-group hypothesis is imposed at this fiber.

ks10:data:polarization.statement: Let q₀,q₁ be rational quadratic Hodge polarizations of the same K3-type Hodge structure T, allowing either overall sign under the stated period-plane convention. If T⊂H²(S,Q) and m^{q₀} is algebraically realized, then m^{q₁} is algebraically realized. No assumption that the polarization-change Hodge endomorphism is scalar or algebraic on S is made.

ks10:conjecture:unrestricted-ks.statement: The unrestricted algebraicity assertion for the Kuga–Satake Hodge embedding is a particular rational Hodge-conjecture problem. The manuscript does not prove existence of its initial algebraic map and explicitly does not claim to resolve the unrestricted Kuga–Satake conjecture.

ks10:input:nonzero-correspondence.statement: There exist an abelian variety B and an actual rational algebraic α∈CH²(S×B)_Q with α_*|_V nonzero. Motivated or absolute Hodge classes alone do not satisfy this existence input.

ks10:input:surface-cover.statement: There exist a smooth connected projective surface Y and a dominant generically finite morphism f:Y→S with nonzero trace on the wedge image Λ²H⁰(Y,Ω¹_Y)→H⁰(Y,Ω²_Y). This is an existence input, equivalent to the correspondence input under Hg(V)=SO(V,q).

ks10:input:very-general-existence.statement: In the chosen degree-2d polarized component, either the actual nonzero-correspondence input or the wedge-trace surface-cover input holds very generally; locally the required quantifier is outside countably many proper closed analytic subsets in a full chart about each desired target.

ks10:import:hodge-theory.statement: For smooth projective complex varieties, Hodge decomposition, Poincaré duality, Lefschetz (1,1), hard Lefschetz and Hodge–Riemann relations hold; pullbacks, Gysin maps and products have their usual Hodge types.

ks10:import:semisimplicity.statement: Polarizable rational Hodge structures have Hodge complements and reductive rational Hodge groups, also for finite joint collections.

ks10:import:algebraic-groups.statement: In characteristic zero, algebraic group homomorphisms have closed image and surjective differential onto its Lie algebra; unipotent groups have nonzero invariants in nonzero representations; a reductive Lie algebra is the sum of its center and simple ideals.

ks10:import:k3-deformations.statement: A complex K3 surface has rank-22 cup lattice and the stated Hodge numbers, a smooth 20-dimensional universal deformation and a local period isomorphism; fixing a nonzero integral (1,1) class cuts out the corresponding period hypersurface and extends its line bundle.

ks10:import:classical-ks.statement: The full even Clifford construction of a polarized K3-type Hodge structure is polarizable of weight one; Clifford multiplication with an invertible right multiplier gives its standard Hodge embedding. No algebraicity theorem for that embedding is an input.

ks10:import:representation-theory.statement: Finite-dimensional representations of complex semisimple Lie algebras are completely reducible and classified by highest weights; type B_n has the dominant/spin weights used in the text. Clifford basis and spin double-cover statements hold in characteristic zero.

ks10:import:weight-one.statement: H¹ contravariantly identifies complex abelian varieties up to isogeny with polarizable rational weight-one Hodge structures; a polarized complex torus is projective.

ks10:import:albanese.statement: For smooth projective complex Y its Albanese is an abelian variety, and an Albanese map induces an isomorphism on holomorphic one-forms.

ks10:import:correspondences.statement: On smooth projective varieties, correspondences compose by pullback, intersection and proper pushforward with the indicated codimension, and cycle classes commute with these operations.

ks10:import:hilbert.statement: For a projective family over a noetherian base, every fixed-polynomial relative Hilbert scheme is projective with a flat universal subscheme; a uniform sufficiently high degree supplies its Grassmannian realization.

ks10:import:smoothness-ample.statement: Flat finitely presented morphisms with smooth fibers are smooth. For proper flat families, the smooth-fiber locus is open. Sufficiently high powers of ample bundles on projective varieties are very ample and have vanishing higher cohomology; Riemann–Roch computes Euler characteristics from Chern classes.

ks10:import:cartier.statement: If a Cartier equation is a nonzerodivisor on a closed subscheme Z of dimension at most k+1, Cartier pullback carries [Z]_{k+1} to the k-dimensional cycle of the cut with scheme multiplicities.

ks10:import:analytic-cohomology.statement: Proper holomorphic maps have coherent higher direct images. For coherent sheaves flat over a reduced base, fiber cohomology is upper semicontinuous; constant dimensions give local freeness and base change. Coherent sheaves on Stein spaces have vanishing higher cohomology.

ks10:import:analytic-proper-images.statement: Proper smooth submersions are locally differentiably trivial. Proper holomorphic images of closed analytic sets are analytic. Irreducible components of complex analytic sets are closed and locally finite, and are countable in a second-countable space.

ks10:import:resolution-gaga.statement: Complex quasi-projective varieties admit projective resolutions. Closed analytic subvarieties of projective space and holomorphic maps of projective varieties are algebraic; projective coherent and analytic cohomology agree.

ks30:ext:criterion.statement: Let S be any projective K3 surface. Suppose that for one rational nonisotropic w∈T_S, one rational weight-one polarization and one full even-Clifford realization H¹(A,Q)=C⁺(T_S,q), the tensor of j_w(v)(a)=vaw is induced by a cycle in CH²(S×A²)_Q. Then rational HC and rational GHC hold in every degree of every self-power S^m.

ks30:main:theorem.statement: Let S be a smooth projective complex K3 surface with a rational isometric embedding of its actual transcendental cup-product space (T_S,q) into V_P. For every full realization H¹(A,Q)=C⁺(T_S,q), every rational nonisotropic w∈T_S and every rational polarization E of that weight-one structure, a cycle Γ_S∈CH²(S×A×A)_Q acts on every x∈T_S as exactly ι_{w,E}(x) in full H²(A²,Q). The same holds for any specified transported isogenous model. Moreover rational HC and GHC hold in every degree of S^m for every m≥1. All ample P-polarized surfaces, including Picard jumps, satisfy the embedding hypothesis.

ks30:main:lattice.statement: P admits a primitive embedding in Λ_K3=U³⊕E₈(−1)² whose integral orthogonal complement is T_P=U⊕U(2)⊕D₄(−1). For every primitive embedding P→Λ_K3, the rational orthogonal complement is isometric to V_P.

ks30:ext:conditional.statement: Let S be projective K3, t=dim_Q T, V=T(1), and W=C⁺(T,q)=H¹(A,Q). Suppose one exact j_w tensor, for rational nonisotropic w and a rational polarization, is induced by CH²(S×A²)_Q. For every 1≤k≤t there is an injective algebraic Hodge map F_k:Λ^kV→End(W) with algebraic left inverse on cohomology. For Z=A² and n=dim Z, it is realized by Γ_k∈CH^{k+1}(S^k×Z)_Q and R_k∈CH^{n+k−1}(Z×S^k)_Q, with R_k*F_k=id using End(W)≅(H¹(A)⊗H¹(A))(1)⊂H²(Z)(1) and Λ^kV⊂H^{2k}(S^k)(k). Every rational Hodge class in Λ^kV is a codimension-k rational algebraic cycle class on S^k.

ks30:ghc:lem:cycle-support.statement: For smooth projective X,Y of dimensions N,D and any C∈CH^{N+p}(X×Y)_Q with p≥0, there is a fixed closed B⊂Y of codimension at least p supporting the entire cohomological image of C. In particular C_*H^j(X,Q)⊂N^pH^{j+2p}(Y,Q) for every j.

ks30:ghc:prop:exterior-coniveau.statement: If S satisfies ext:conditional's exact even-Clifford algebraicity premise, then for every 1≤k≤t=dim_Q T, Λ^kT⊂N^{k−1}H^{2k}(S^k,Q). Every rational sub-Hodge structure of this exterior power satisfies GHC in that ambient cohomology. In particular the top exterior line Λ^tT is supported in codimension t.

ks30:ghc:lem:orthogonal-carriers.statement: Let V=T(1) for a projective K3 with Hg(V)=SO(V,q), t=dim V≥3. Let H be a nontrivial rational simple representation occurring in a direct sum of tensor powers of V, with its induced weight-zero Hodge structure of Hodge level at most 2b. Then there are c,s≥1 and integers 1≤k_i≤t with c≤b and s=Σk_i, and a surjective rational Hodge map ⊗_{i=1}^c Λ^{k_i}V→H.

ks30:ghc:lem:k3-carriers.statement: For V=T(1) of any projective K3 and G=Hg(V), let H be a nontrivial rational simple G-representation occurring in a direct sum of tensor powers of V, with induced Hodge level at most 2b. Then for some 1≤c≤b and 1≤k₁,…,k_c≤dim_Q V there is a surjective rational Hodge map ⊗_{j=1}^cΛ^{k_j}V→H. The claim includes totally real and CM endomorphism fields, rational nonsplit forms and all actual rational constituents.

ks30:geom:structure.statement: For the stated smooth abelian double-cover data there is a smooth double cover Y→K=Km(B'), K resolved, such that: (i) V=H²(Y,Z)^{δ=−1} modulo torsion is even of signature (2,14) with 2-elementary discriminant group, and fixed-(B,M,χ) monodromy is trivial on that group; (ii) eight mutually orthogonal algebraic anti-invariant classes a_i of square −4 have perpendicular U⊂V_Q of signature (2,6), rationally isometric to V_P with the Y intersection form; (iii) resolved pullback gives a flat Hodge isomorphism β:U≅U_X with (βx,βy)_X=2(x,y)_Y, and e=(Δ_X+Γ_j−Γ_δ−Γ_{jδ})/4∈CH²(X×X)_Q has image U_X in degree two and vanishes in every other degree. All constructions are compatible with the indicated smooth parameter opens.

ks30:geom:twisted-hodge.statement: Set E=T_B(−log D). U_X admits a flat complex identification with a character eigenspace having U_X^{p,q}≅H^q(B,Ω_B^p(log D)⊗M^−1χ), p+q=2; in particular U_X^{2,0}=H⁰(B,Mχ) is one-dimensional. Fix a nonzero invariant volume form Ω and a generator θ of H⁰(B,Mχ). The period differential is induced on H¹ by E→E⊗Mχ≅Ω_B¹(log D)⊗M^−1χ, multiplication by θ. The full six-dimensional family tangent space identifies with H¹(B,E) by Kodaira–Spencer.

ks30:geom:period.statement: The period map of U, equivalently U_X, has rank six on a nonempty Zariski-open subset of the six-dimensional parameter space. For very general parameters U is simple, has no nonzero rational (1,1) class, and has Hodge group SO(U).

ks30:geom:gauss-generic.statement: On a nonempty Zariski-open set of (B,D) parameters, D has no nontrivial translation stabilizer, C=D/{±1} is smooth of genus three, and D→C is a connected étale double cover defined by nontrivial ε∈Pic⁰(C)[2]. The Gauss map factors D→C→P¹ with degrees two and four, the latter map given by |K_C⊗ε|. No fiber of that degree-four map has all multiplicities even. The good open remains nonempty on every component after the finite theta, torsion and level choices defining X.

ks30:geom:halves.statement: There is an algebraic h:Selections→B with 2h(s)=Σ_{p∈s}p and h(s[p])=h(s)−p. The selection cover splits globally by parity into degree-eight covers S_+ and S_−. Their possibly disconnected smooth projective completions C_± carry extensions a_±:C_±→B. At every point where a_± has nonzero differential it is tangent to the direction recorded by its P¹ parameter.

ks30:geom:relations.statement: On a regular-value disc, no signed sum of a nonempty subset of the four local branches x_i is constant. Every connected component of C_± maps nonconstantly to B. No image component Z_+ from C_+ and Z_− from C_− satisfies Z_+=b−Z_− for any b∈B.

ks30:geom:domination.statement: For every parameter in a nonempty Zariski-open subset there exist smooth projective connected curves C₁,C₂ and a dominant generically finite morphism g:C₁×C₂→X. If additionally U_X has no nonzero rational (1,1) class, an algebraic correspondence injects U_X into H¹(C₁,Q)⊗H¹(C₂,Q). Thus the injection exists at very general parameters.

ks30:geom:genericity.statement: Every nonempty regular period chart admits a smaller normalized product chart A×Q of abelian data and affine section coordinates in the simultaneous geometric open of geom:period and geom:domination. Given any countable collection of proper closed analytic period loci in the original chart, one can successively choose: abelian data a in a residual subset of A; for each such a, a section pencil in a residual subset of each prescribed nonempty admissible pencil open meeting Q; then, after fixing that pencil, all but countably many points of its intersection with Q and a nonempty algebraic good open. These points avoid the prescribed loci. Proper marked rational Hodge-tensor exceptions on the connected smooth pencil part are countable. The pencils are d_t=d₀+t d₁ with ℓ(d₀)=1, ℓ(d₁)=0 and d₁ smooth avoiding two-torsion. Further pencil-specific countable exclusions may be added after the pencil is fixed; no uniform exceptional list across pencils is claimed.

ks30:pencil:realization.statement: Choose abelian data and d_t=d₀+t d₁ in geom:genericity's generic sets. There is a nonempty algebraic O⊂A¹_t and a smooth projective K3 family S⁰→O with a flat isometric embedding U→R²(S⁰/O)_*Q, using U's cup form inherited from Y. For very general t, U_t is the entire transcendental part of H²(S⁰_t,Q). For every s in a nonempty Zariski-open subset of A¹_s, every smooth projective model of the total family pulled back by t=s+u² is uniruled. The K3 family is defined over the original t-line; no unspecified finite base change remains.

ks30:pencil:lattice.statement: Let V be an even lattice of signature (2,14) with elementary 2-primary discriminant group, and G⊂O(V) act trivially on that group. Then there exist an even finite-index overlattice M of V, a primitive embedding M→Λ_K3, and a primitive positive h∈M-perpendicular such that G extends to Λ_K3 acting identically on M-perpendicular.

ks30:pencil:monodromy.statement: For the general normalized section pencil with fixed abelian data and smooth leading section avoiding two-torsion, monodromy on V at every finite singular parameter is a product of reflections in mutually orthogonal integral (−2)-roots in V, perpendicular to the limiting Hodge line. After killing those finite monodromies, the periods extend to interior periods. At infinity monodromy on V is −id.

ks30:pencil:periodstack.statement: There is a morphism q:P_h=[Γ_h\D_h]→M_h, the moduli stack of primitively polarized ADE K3 surfaces of degree (h,h), whose composite with the smooth quasi-polarized period map is canonical polarized contraction. Pullback of the Hodge line is the tautological period line with its full Γ_h-linearization. At [σ], the stabilizer-map kernel is exactly the group W_σ generated by reflections in roots r∈Λ_K3 with r²=−2, (r,h)=0 and (r,σ)=0.

ks30:pencil:descent.statement: Let C be a smooth projective complex curve, D⊂C finite, C°=C\D. Suppose (i) L is a Λ_K3 local system on C° with flat positive primitive h; (ii) a holomorphic line F⊂L⊗O has (F,F)=0, (σ,bar σ)>0 for nonzero σ∈F, and (F,h)=0; (iii) every puncture has finite local monodromy and an interior limiting period after a killing cover. Then a normal projective model Z→C restricts on C° to a polarized ADE K3 family realizing the data modulo contracted roots. If at every puncture monodromy is in the Weyl group generated by roots perpendicular to h and the limiting F, Z→C may be flat ADE everywhere, its Hodge line descends to λ on C, and ω_{Z/C}=f*λ, K_Z=f*(K_C⊗λ). Independently of this extra Weyl condition, if nondegenerate U⊂L_Q contains F and every locally flat root persistently of type (1,1) is perpendicular to U, then on a smaller nonempty algebraic open of C° there is a smooth projective K3 family S⁰ realizing U isometrically as a Hodge summand, without changing C.

ks30:pencil:uniruledcriterion.statement: Under the Weyl condition in pencil:descent, if deg(K_C⊗λ)<0, every smooth projective model of the function field of Z is uniruled.

ks30:comp:twosquares.statement: Let O⊂A¹_t be nonempty Zariski open and S→O, X→O smooth projective families of connected surfaces, with S fibers K3. Assume: (i) a polarized rational K3-type subvariation U⊂R²f_*Q has nondegenerate restricted cup form, nonconstant period, and simple fibers outside a countable set; (ii) commuting involutions j,δ on X give e=(1+j)(1−δ)/4 annihilating R^qg_*Q for q≠2, with a specified VHS isomorphism φ:U≅eR²g_*Q; (iii) for s in a nonempty Zariski open, both total families pulled back by t=s+u² have smooth projective uniruled threefold models. Then there are nonempty Zariski-open G⊂O and countable E⊂G such that every b∈G\E has Θ_b∈CH²(S_b×X_b)_Q inducing exactly φ_b on U_b. G and all auxiliaries used before choosing b can be fixed for that pencil.

ks30:comp:uniruled.statement: For a smooth projective uniruled complex threefold Z, H³(Z) is a direct summand of a finite sum of H¹(C_i)(−1) for smooth projective curves, with both splitting maps algebraic. Consequently every rational Hodge map between H³ of two such threefolds is algebraic.

ks30:comp:affine.statement: For a smooth affine complex curve B: (i) every bounded complex of rational sheaves with finite-rank local-system cohomology only in even degrees has a unique splitting into its shifted cohomology sheaves inducing the identity on each; (ii) every bounded complex A with local-system cohomology has the natural exact sequence 0→H¹(B,H^{n−1}A)→hyperH^n(B,A)→H⁰(B,H^nA)→0 for every n. A morphism's action on the left term is determined by its map on H^{n−1}.

ks30:comp:hodgelift.statement: Let I be a smooth affine curve, E^S→I a smooth projective K3 family, and E^X→I a smooth projective surface family with a relative algebraic idempotent e acting on the direct-image complex and annihilating R^q for q≠2. Given a rational VHS morphism a:R²h_S*Q→eR²h_X*Q and smooth projective compactifications Z^S,Z^X extending the maps to the compactified curve and unchanged over I, there is a rational Hodge map c:H³(Z^S)→H³(Z^X) such that e res_X(cz)=H¹(I,a)(res_S z), using the canonical H³(E^S)=H¹(I,R²h_S*Q) and eH³(E^X)=H¹(I,eR²h_X*Q) identifications.

ks30:comp:models.statement: For a smooth projective surface family Y→O in this section, the first square pullbacks admit models Z projective over A¹_s and nonempty open G⊂O with Z_G→G smooth. For every b∈G one can choose a smooth projective fourfold M_b mapping to P¹_t and P¹_v whose inverse images of V₀={v∈A¹:b+v²∈G} and O are respectively Z_G×_G V₀ (s=b+v²) and Y×_O Q_b, Q_b={u²+v²=(t−b)w²}⊂O×P². These identifications agree on their intersection and both are actual preserved opens. Shrinking G before b is chosen preserves the conclusions.

ks30:comp:surface.statement: Fix abelian-cover data and a section pencil satisfying geom:structure, geom:period and pencil:realization, with nonconstant U-period along it and simple U_t outside a countable set. On a nonempty open of that pencil, for all but countably many b, there exists Θ_b∈CH²(S⁰_b×X_b)_Q inducing on U_b the specified identification with H²(X_b)^{j=+,δ=−}.

ks30:final:curves.statement: Choose abelian data and a pencil as in geom:genericity, then b in the common good open outside the countable exceptions of that lemma and comp:surface. Then smooth projective curves C₁,C₂ and Z∈CH²(S⁰_b×C₁×C₂)_Q exist whose action injects U_b→H¹(C₁,Q)⊗H¹(C₂,Q). Here U_b=T_{S⁰_b} and Hg(U_b)=SO(U_b).

ks30:final:spin.statement: Let (U,q) be eight-dimensional polarized rational K3 type of signature (2,6), Hg(U)=SO(U,q), W_i polarized effective weight one, and W=C⁺(U,q) with its KS structure. For every nonzero rational Hodge f:U→W₁⊗W₂, set H=Hom_HS(W₁,W)⊗Hom_HS(W₂,W). The map Φ:H⊕H→Hom_HS(U,W⊗W), (a⊗b,0)↦(a⊗b)f and (0,a⊗b)↦τ(a⊗b)f with ordinary flip τ, is surjective. If U⊂H²(M,Q) for a smooth projective surface, W_i=H¹(C_i,Q), W=H¹(A,Q), and f is induced by a codimension-two cycle M→C₁×C₂, every target map is induced by CH²(M×A×A)_Q.

ks30:final:generic.statement: Let b be a construction point of final:curves. If a projective K3 S admits a rational Hodge isometry r_T:T_S≅U_b=T_{S⁰_b} for their cup forms, then for every full even-Clifford A for T_S, every rational nonisotropic right factor w and every rational polarization E, there is Γ_S∈CH²(S×A×A)_Q with Γ_S*x=ι_{w,E}(x) for all x∈T_S, as equality in the full H²(A²,Q).

ks30:specialization:ambient.statement: For every K3 S with an ample primitive P-polarization, put U_P=P_Q-perpendicular⊂H²(S,Q). There exist a full W_U=C⁺(U_P,q)=H¹(A_U,Q), rational polarization E₀, rational nonisotropic w₀∈U_P, and Γ_U∈CH²(S×A_U²)_Q whose entire degree-two action on every x∈U_P is exactly ι_{w₀,E₀}(x), including the rational (1,1) classes in U_P at a Picard jump.

ks30:final:hilbert.statement: Let f:Z→B be a smooth proper holomorphic family of pure dimension n over a connected coordinate ball, with a closed relative embedding into P^N×B. Fix 0≤r≤n, a rational local system V, a morphism L:R^{2r}f_*Q→V, and a flat τ∈H⁰(B,V). The points b admitting a rational codimension-r cycle Z_b with L_b(cl(Z_b))=τ_b form a countable union of closed analytic subsets, each the image of a proper analytic parameter space carrying a fixed rational combination of universal flat subschemes; every point supplies an actual successful cycle. If that successful set contains a nonempty open, or escapes every countable union of proper closed analytic subsets, it equals B.

ks30:specialization:rational-density.statement: For every rational quadratic (V,q) of signature (2,n), O(V)(Q) is dense in O(V_R), and the rational orthogonal orbit of every point of its type-IV period domain meets every nonempty open subset of that domain.

ks30:transfer:compression.statement: Let i:W_T→W_U be an inclusion of polarizable rational weight-one Hodge structures, p:W_U→W_T a Hodge retraction, E_U,E_T rational polarizations, H a rational weight-zero Hodge structure, and j:H→End(W_U) a Hodge map. Put b=(E_T^flat)^−1 i∨(−1) E_U^flat. For the tensor form ι_{j,E_U}:H(−1)→W_U⊗W_U, (p⊗b)ι_{j,E_U}=ι_{pji,E_T}. When the weight-one spaces are abelian H¹, both slot maps are induced by rational algebraic correspondences.

ks30:transfer:ample.statement: For every ample P-polarized K3 S and every prescribed rational nonisotropic w∈T_S, rational polarization E and transported full even-Clifford realization C⁺(T_S,q), the exact standard ι_{w,E} admits a rational codimension-two algebraic realization.

ks30:transfer:period.statement: If a projective K3 S has a rational isometric embedding T_S→V_P, there is an ample P-polarized K3 R and a full rational Hodge isometry Φ:H²(S,Q)≅H²(R,Q) with Φ(T_S)=T_R. Both Φ and Φ^−1 are induced by algebraic correspondences.

ks30:transfer:tensor.statement: Under main:theorem's rational isometric-embedding hypothesis, the exact tensor ι_{w,E} on T_S is algebraic for every stipulated w, E and transported isogenous full even-Clifford model.

ks30:transfer:moduli.statement: For every smooth projective complex K3 S with (T_S,q) rationally isometrically embedded in V_P, every n,r≥1 has HC and GHC in every degree of (S^[n])^r. More generally, for α∈Br(S), if M is a smooth projective moduli space of Gieseker-stable α-twisted sheaves on S, or of σ-stable objects in D^b(S,α) for a generic Bridgeland stability σ, then HC and GHC hold in every degree of M^r for every r≥1. If M is hyperkähler, the same holds for every smooth projective hyperkähler variety birational to M and all its self-powers.

ks30:conjecture:hc.statement: For every smooth projective complex X and every r, the rational cycle class CH^r(X)_Q→H^{2r}(X,Q)∩H^{r,r}(X) is surjective. The manuscript claims this only for its stated K3 powers and transferred varieties, not for all X.

ks30:conjecture:ghc.statement: For every smooth projective complex X, degree j and coniveau p, N^pH^j(X,Q) equals the largest rational sub-Hodge structure whose types (a,b) have a,b≥p. The manuscript's conclusions are restricted to its stated families.

ks30:input:one-exact-tensor.statement: For a general projective K3 outside any asserted locus, algebraicity of one exact tensor of j_w(v)(a)=vaw on the full C⁺(T_S,q), with one rational nonisotropic w and one rational polarization, is the premise of ext:criterion. An arbitrary nonzero algebraic Hodge embedding, or an absolutely Hodge/motivated tensor without a cycle, is not that premise.

ks30:input:quadratic-embedding.statement: The locus hypothesis is the existence of a rational isometric embedding (T_S,q_cup)→V_P. It concerns the actual cup form, not merely rank, signature, an abstract Hodge embedding, or a differently rescaled form.

ks30:import:absolute-motivated-ks.statement: The classical KS construction produces the relevant abelian varieties and distinguished Hodge correspondence; that correspondence is absolutely Hodge and motivated. Algebraicity of the specified map is an additional assertion, not supplied by these imports.

ks30:import:zarhin.statement: For a projective K3's simple transcendental T, E=End_Hdg(T) is a number field, totally real or CM. The q-adjoint is respectively identity or conjugation. In the totally real case a nondegenerate symmetric E-form φ has trace q and Hg(T(1))=Res_{E/Q}SO(T,φ); in the CM case φ is Hermitian over E/E⁺ and Hg(T(1))=Res_{E⁺/Q}U(T,φ), the full unitary group. Hodge tensors are the invariants of these rational groups.

ks30:import:buskin.statement: Every full rational Hodge isometry H²(S,Q)≅H²(S',Q) between smooth projective complex K3 surfaces is induced by a rational codimension-two algebraic correspondence. The source does not require integrality, preservation of an ample chamber, or equality of integral Néron–Severi lattices. Transcendental isometries are first extended by Witt to full H² isometries.

ks30:import:invariant-generation.statement: Over a splitting algebraic closure, SO invariants in arbitrary tensor powers of its nondegenerate standard module are spanned by metric contractions and a volume tensor. GL invariants on standard and dual slots are spanned by complete pair contractions, with equal numbers of standard and dual slots. The claimed spanning assertions have no stable-range restriction.

ks30:import:period-contraction.statement: For primitive ample ADE polarizations, primitive big-and-nef smooth polarizations and the full integral period stack over C, the source imports existence/factorization of contraction q and the representable surjective étale quasi-polarized period map. The full Hodge-line linearization and exact stabilizer kernel in pencil:periodstack are additional arguments in this manuscript, not silently attributed to the existence theorem.

ks30:import:bdpp.statement: For the smooth projective threefold resolution in pencil:uniruledcriterion, non-pseudoeffectivity of its canonical class implies uniruledness; the source then uses birational invariance to pass to all smooth projective models.

ks30:import:invariant-cycles.statement: For the smooth projective relative product over I and a smooth projective compactification, the image of compactification H⁴ in a fiber is the monodromy-invariant part. Because restriction is a map of polarizable pure Hodge structures, a flat rational (2,2) fiber tensor has a rational (2,2) lift. The lift is not asserted algebraic before the uniruled-threefold argument.

ks30:import:fixed-part-lowest-weight.statement: The invariant part of a geometric polarized variation is a constant Hodge subvariation. Restriction from a smooth projective compactification to a smooth open has image the lowest weight; in the application eH³(E_s^X) has pure polarizable W₃ part T_s, onto which the projected compactification H³ maps.

ks30:import:mhs-localization.statement: For the disjoint smooth divisor boundary D⊂Y^X, localization H²(D)(−1)→H⁴(Y^X)→H⁴(Y^X\D) is exact in canonical mixed Hodge structures. Proper Gysin and restriction are mixed-Hodge morphisms with codimension-one shift [−2](−1), and lowest-weight cohomology is polarizable. Strictness later controls the weight-four boundary error.

ks30:import:leading-chern-character.statement: On a smooth ambient fiber, a coherent sheaf supported in codimension at least r has degree-r Chern character equal to its codimension-r fundamental cycle with generic lengths. GRR, dévissage and algebraic/topological Chern-class compatibility supply this identity; supports of codimension at least r+1 contribute no cohomology below degree 2r+2. The manuscript separately argues that the universal sheaf has the required resolution and restriction behavior over singular Hilbert parameters.

ks30:import:hilbert-motive.statement: The rational Chow motive h(S^[n]) decomposes into Tate twists of summands of motives of powers of S; symmetric-product summands use rational averaging projectors.

ks30:import:moduli-motive.statement: For either smooth projective (possibly twisted) stable-sheaf or generic Bridgeland-stable moduli space M specified in transfer:moduli, h(M) is a summand of a finite sum of Tate twists of h(S^k); tensoring the split correspondences gives the corresponding statements for self-powers.

ks30:import:motivic-hc-ghc-transfer.statement: The source invokes Arapura's transfer lemma to pass HC and GHC for every power of S to varieties motivated by S through the specified Tate-twisted split correspondences, retaining the geometric-coniveau shifts.

ks30:import:birational-hyperkahler.statement: Birational smooth projective hyperkähler varieties have an isomorphism of rational Chow motives supplied by Rieß's specialization correspondence, in the formulation cited from Bülles.

ks30:conjecture:ks-algebraicity.statement: The additional algebraicity assertion requires a cycle inducing the prescribed K3-to-abelian Clifford tensor, not just some algebraic Hodge embedding. The introduction distinguishes these two assertions and cites Floccari–Fu's Conjectures 2.4 and 2.6; this manuscript proves its exact-map assertion only under its stated locus hypothesis and uses it conditionally for arbitrary projective K3 surfaces.

milne:thm:main.statement: Let A/Qbar have dimension d and good reduction A₀/F at w, let 0≤r≤d, and let γ∈H^{2r}(A(C),Q(r)) be rational Hodge. For every list of Cartier divisors D₁,…,D_{d−r} on A₀ there is q∈Q such that Tr_ℓ(γ_{0,ℓ}∏c₁,ℓ(D_i))=q in Q_ℓ for every ℓ≠p and Tr_p(γ_{0,p}∏c₁,cris(D_i))=q in C_w. Here γ_{0,p}∈H^{2r}_cris(A₀/W(F))[1/p](r)⊗_{K₀}C_w and traces send zero-cycle classes to degrees. For r=d the product is 1. This covers all p including 2, divisors that do not lift, and by linearity complementary rational Lefschetz classes.

milne:lem:comparison.statement: For an abelian variety with good reduction, realizations of an absolute Hodge class are compatible with de Rham and crystalline comparisons; the tensor obtained from its p-adic étale realization equals, after scalar extension, its de Rham–crystalline realization in thm:main. This respects tensor operations, duals, Tate twists, divisors and rational homomorphisms. The same applies to good-reduction auxiliaries over a finite extension of K₀, using an abstract complex embedding of an algebraic closure of their definition field.

milne:lem:pairing-functorial.statement: If a tuple α has the Lefschetz pairing property on an abelian variety Y/F and f∈Hom⁰(X,Y), then f*α has it on X. The claim allows arbitrary rational homomorphisms, not just isogenies; degree-out-of-range cases give zero.

milne:lem:lift-hom.statement: Let R be a complete mixed-characteristic DVR finite over W(F), K its fraction field, X,Y abelian schemes over R and f₀∈Hom⁰(X₀,Y₀). If the contravariant crystalline map of this specified rational algebraic f₀ preserves the Hodge filtrations, f₀ lifts uniquely to a rational homomorphism X→Y. A symmetric such X₀→X₀∨ lifts to a rational divisor class on the generic fiber (after finite extension if needed in the proof). Algebraic identities among finitely many lifted maps remain valid. No arbitrary Q_p-linear cohomology map is asserted algebraic.

milne:prop:transport.statement: Let A/Qbar have positive dimension and good reduction, V=H₁(A(C),Q), and G⊂GSp(V,ψ) be connected reductive with Hodge homomorphism h of A and a conjugacy class X making this a Hodge embedding. Suppose γ is rational Hodge of codimension r whose alternating form satisfies γ(gv₁,…,gv_{2r})=c(g)^rγ(v₁,…,v_{2r}) for G's multiplier c. Then there are n>0, a good-reduction B, one quasi-isogeny a:A₀^n→B₀ and rational Hodge κ of codimension r with (aj)*κ₀=γ₀, simultaneously for every ℓ≠p and crystalline cohomology extended to C_w, j the first-factor inclusion. One may require either (1) B CM over Qbar at w; or (2) given a degree-(0,1) weakly admissible filtration F_A on D_A=H¹_cris(A₀)[1/p] over finite K/K₀, having finite local-field descent with the G-tensors and geometrically in the G-orbit of the original filtration under a tensor-preserving identification, B is over a finite extension K/K₀ inside C_w and a*Fil¹H¹_dR(B)=(F_A¹)^⊕n after common finite extension. In (2) choose a complex embedding extending Qbar; κ's realizations use canonical model tensors and polarization. In (1) they equal its usual absolute-Hodge realizations.

milne:lem:auxiliary-datum.statement: Given a Hodge embedding (G,X)→(GSp(V,ψ),Siegel) with G connected and multiplier c, for every prime p there exist a totally real P, connected reductive J and Hodge embedding (J,X_J)→GSp(W,ψ_W) such that: (i) G→J→Res_{P/Q}G_P are Shimura-data inclusions, first diagonal, and J imposes equal similitude multipliers; (ii) J_Qp is quasi-split and has a full connected stabilizer J_model making the triple strongly admissible; (iii) W≅(V⊗_Q P)^⊕m as rational J-representation for some m>0, ψ_W has common multiplier c, and J_model→GL(W_Qp) extends to a closed immersion into GL(Λ_p) for a self-dual Z_p lattice.

milne:lem:admissible-realization.statement: Let (J,X_J,J_model) be strongly admissible with J_Qp quasi-split, using the adapted embedding and neat level, and let x∈S_K(F) have a characteristic-zero lift. Suppose a filtration F on D_x over finite extension of K₀ is admissible and geometrically induced by a J-valued cocharacter in the X_J conjugacy class. After a further finite extension there exist y∈I_x, a single tensor-preserving quasi-isogeny b:C_x→C_y and a lift y~ over the extended valuation ring such that b*Fil¹H¹_dR(C_y~)=F¹. Admissibility follows in particular from weak admissibility plus finite local-field descent of the filtered isocrystal and tensor data.

milne:cor:cm-transport.statement: For every positive-dimensional A/Qbar with good reduction at w and rational Hodge γ∈H^{2r}(A(C),Q(r)), 0≤r≤dim A, there are n>0, a CM abelian B/Qbar with good reduction, a rational Hodge κ of codimension r and one quasi-isogeny a:A₀^n→B₀ with γ₀=(aj)*κ₀, j first-factor inclusion. This is one equality of usual absolute-Hodge specializations in every prime-to-p realization and crystalline cohomology extended to C_w.

milne:thm:filtration.statement: Let A₀/F have a rational CM-field E action and a polarization whose Rosati induces conjugation on E. Suppose D=H¹_cris(A₀/W(F))[1/p] has rank 2s over E⊗K₀ with s≥1, and some invertible u∈End⁰(A₀) satisfies u†=u and ue=bar e u for all e∈E. Let β be the dual polarization into the slope-one isocrystal line. Then there are finite K/K₀ and L⊂D_K whose degree-(0,1) filtration is weakly admissible, with L E- and u-stable and β-Lagrangian, dim_Ω L_τ=s for every E-embedding over every algebraically closed Ω/K, and finite local-field descent of the indicated filtered tensor data. Geometrically all balanced E-stable β-Lagrangians form one orbit under G_D={g∈GSp(D,β)∩GL_{E⊗K₀}(D):det_{E⊗K₀}g=c(g)^s}; each is the weight-one subspace of a weights-(0,1) cocharacter of G_D. In particular L belongs to any original balanced polarized filtration orbit under tensor-preserving comparison.

milne:lem:avoidance.statement: For every finite K₁/K₀ and integers r,b≥1, there exist θ algebraic over Q_p and (x₀,…,x_{r−1})∈K₁(θ)^r such that every nonzero polynomial in K₁[X₀,…,X_{r−1}] of total degree at most b is nonzero at that point. All x_i may be chosen in Q_p(θ). The coefficient field is the fixed K₁, not K₁(θ).

milne:lem:lagrangian-intersection.statement: Let M be a 2m-dimensional symplectic space over characteristic-zero k, and W⊂M have dimension a. A nonempty open subset of its Lagrangian Grassmannian consists of L with dim(L∩W)=max(0,a−m). On any fixed symplectic affine big cell, some nonzero polynomial of degree at most m has nonvanishing locus contained in that open; this degree bound is independent of W.

milne:cor:filtration-admissible.statement: The filtration constructed in thm:filtration, with its finite local-field descent, is admissible: its descended filtered isocrystal is the filtered crystalline module of a crystalline representation.

milne:cor:filtration-divisor.statement: For D,L from thm:filtration, let ψ and U be the homological polarization and u-action on D_K∨. The untwisted divisor form ψ(−,U−) belongs to Fil¹(Λ²D_K)=L∧D_K and hence to filtration degree zero after the codimension-one Tate twist. If a marked power is realized by an abelian lift, the corresponding pulled-back divisor satisfies lem:lift-hom's filtration condition for its symmetric homomorphism.

milne:prop:weil.statement: For every γ∈W_E^s(A) in the balanced good-reduction setting, γ₀ has the Lefschetz pairing property at w. More precisely, if U={u∈End⁰(A₀):u†=u, ue=bar e u for all e∈E} has no invertible element, all complementary pairings vanish. If U has an invertible element, γ₀ is one simultaneous rational Lefschetz class, not merely locally divisor-generated in separate realizations.

milne:lem:weil-orthogonality.statement: If the rational anti-linear Rosati-symmetric space U has no invertible element, every specialization of every class in W_E^s(A) pairs to zero with every complementary Lefschetz class, in each realization.

milne:lem:weil-divisor-span.statement: Let B be complex abelian, R∈End⁰(B) an idempotent and E→R End⁰(B)R an algebra action with unit R. Let T=im(R) on rational first homology have E-dimension 2s, with those endomorphisms zero on ker R. Suppose a rational divisor D has R*D=D and, over a splitting field, D=Σ_τD_τ with D_τ∈Λ²T_τ∨⊗Q(1) nondegenerate, with no cross-embedding terms. Then the rational subspace whose extension is ⊕_τΛ^{2s}T_τ∨⊗Q(s), extended by zero on the complementary summand, consists of rational Lefschetz classes on B.

milne:lem:weil-group.statement: The Hodge homomorphism of balanced A factors through G={a∈GSp(V,ψ)∩GL_E(V):det_E a=c(a)^s}, and its conjugacy class defines a Hodge-type Shimura datum via that embedding. Over an algebraically closed field the corresponding filtration orbit on H¹ consists exactly of E-stable Lagrangians for the dual polarization having dimension s at every embedding. With a Tate-line basis, every determinant form in eq:weil-pure-space transforms by c^s.

milne:lem:cm-reduction.statement: For every CM abelian A/Qbar with good reduction at w, r>0 and rational Hodge γ∈H^{2r}(A(C),Q(r)), there are finitely many good-reduction B_i/Qbar, rational homomorphisms f_i:A→B_i and rational Weil classes η_i∈H^{2r}(B_i(C),Q(r)) with γ=Σf_i*η_i. Each B_i has a CM-field K action with H₁ of K-rank 2r, Hodge signatures (r,r) at every embedding and a polarization inducing conjugation on K. The equality specializes with the same rational coefficients in every realization in thm:main. The proof constructs these via rational-idempotent factors of actual powers of A; it uses only balanced signatures, not split Weil type.

milne:cor:cm-pairing.statement: The specialization of every rational Hodge class on a CM abelian variety over Qbar with good reduction at w has the Lefschetz pairing property.

milne:cor:all-hodge-specialization.statement: With p,w and one good rational Tate-class theory R fixed before varying A, for every good-reduction abelian A/Qbar of dimension d, 0≤r≤d and rational Hodge γ∈H^{2r}(A(C),Q(r)), there exists a unique ρ_γ∈R^r(A₀) satisfying (ρ_γ)_ℓ=γ_{0,ℓ} for all ℓ≠p and (ρ_γ)_p⊗1=γ_{0,p} over C_w. This holds for every p, including 2. Uniqueness is in that fixed cohomological theory, not in the Chow group.

milne:cor:algebraic-specialization.statement: Using the additional CM Hodge theorem OpenAICMHodge2026, Theorem 1.1, for every good-reduction A/Qbar of dimension d and rational Hodge γ∈H^{2r}(A(C),Q(r)), 0≤r≤d, there is one z_γ∈CH^r(A₀)_Q whose ℓ-adic classes equal γ_{0,ℓ} for all ℓ≠p and whose crystalline class extended to C_w equals γ_{0,p}. This holds for all p including 2. For every y∈CH^{d−r}(A₀)_Q, all corresponding trace pairings equal deg(z_γ·y)∈Q. The representing Chow class is not claimed unique, no lift of it to A is claimed, and no arbitrary characteristic-zero abelian HC is concluded.

milne:conjecture:rationality.statement: Milne's pairing rationality asks that after good reduction a rational Hodge class have rational complementary divisor-product pairings, with one rational value in all realizations even for new nonlifting divisors. The manuscript states its precise claimed solution in thm:main; its cited antecedent pairing formulation is Milne2009 Conjecture 4.1 and MilneAIM2007 Section 10.

milne:conjecture:weak-rationality.statement: As described here, weak rationality asks that a specialized CM Hodge class whose components lie in the local spans of divisor products in every realization arise from one rational Lefschetz class. Only this manuscript's description is inventoried; the external full conjecture has not been read.

milne:question:simultaneous-lift.statement: The source describes Milne's question whether a specialized CM Hodge class and a divisor lift together, up to isogeny, to a CM variety, and a conditional rationality criterion through weak lifting of Lefschetz classes on CM Weil triples. These are historical antecedents, not assumptions substituted for this manuscript's local prescribed-filtration construction; the source does not reproduce the full external statements.

milne:input:prescribed-filtration.statement: Transport alternative (2) requires a degree-(0,1) weakly admissible filtration on D_A over a finite extension of K₀, finite local-field descent together with the specialized G-structure tensors, and membership after geometric tensor-preserving identification in the G-orbit of the original Hodge filtration. Weak admissibility alone without these other hypotheses is not the stated input.

milne:input:invertible-rosati.statement: The filtration theorem requires an invertible rational endomorphism u of the reduced abelian variety, Rosati self-adjoint and conjugate-linear over the given CM field: ue=bar e u for all e. The main argument does not assume such a u always exists: prop:weil treats its nonexistence by a zero-pairing branch.

milne:import:cm-hodge-theorem.statement: The source invokes OpenAI's 'The rational Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties', Theorem 1.1, to represent every rational Hodge class on the complex CM auxiliary B by a rational algebraic cycle. This is an additional input solely to cor:algebraic-specialization, not to the rationality theorem or CM transport. That October 6 manuscript was not among the assigned sources and was not read.

milne:import:absolute-hodge.statement: Every Hodge class on an abelian variety is absolute Hodge; its p-adic realization has the comparison compatibility invoked in lem:comparison, including the perfect-residue-field version for local auxiliary lifts. This supplies compatible realizations, not rational intersections with new divisors by itself.

milne:import:lefschetz-algebra.statement: For an abelian X/F, Lef^r(X) realizes injectively and its scalar extension is the divisor-generated subspace in every relevant cohomology, including crystalline. Intersection gives a perfect rational pairing with Lef^{dim X−r}; homomorphism pushforward preserves local divisor-generated subspaces; hard Lefschetz and its inverse restrict to them. Extension from crystalline coefficients to C_w preserves these statements.

milne:import:filtered-dieudonne.statement: For the good-reduction abelian schemes over a complete mixed-characteristic DVR with perfect residue field, full faithfulness of rational filtered Dieudonné modules is invoked to turn a Frobenius-compatible filtration-preserving crystalline map into a rational map of p-divisible groups (equivalently of Tate modules via crystalline comparison). The input in lem:lift-hom is already a rational algebraic special-fiber homomorphism.

milne:import:tate-extension.statement: After one integer clears both the Tate-lattice and prescribed f₀ denominators, Tate's extension theorem extends the resulting integral generic-fiber p-divisible-group map over R. Faithfulness of the special-fiber Dieudonné functor and torsion-freeness identify its reduction with Nf₀.

milne:import:serre-tate-formal.statement: Specified-map Serre–Tate deformation theory supplies compatible lifts over R/m^n of an algebraic special-fiber homomorphism together with the matching p-divisible-group lift. Formal existence algebraizes the resulting map when its source is proper over the complete noetherian R and target separated of finite type. The source's shear argument connects the fixed-object formulation to specified maps.

milne:import:adapted-embedding.statement: For the constructed strongly admissible Hodge datum, the source applies the adapted symplectic embedding theorem to obtain a self-dual Z_p lattice and integral closed immersion. It asserts the rational representation built in that theorem stays a sum of copies of U=V⊗P and that p=2 is included using the reduced-relative-root condition. The copy-preservation assertion is explicitly read off from the cited proof in the manuscript, not externally checked here.

milne:import:canonical-tensors.statement: At neat prime-to-p level and the adapted parahoric level, the source invokes the Hodge-type integral model, universal abelian scheme, defining tensors and compatible Betti/étale/crystalline frame torsors. It then extends any added rational J-invariant tensor by evaluating it in those torsors and argues comparison and a single tensor-preserving quasi-isogeny preserve all such tensors simultaneously. Only the canonical sections/torsors are the imported input; the extension-to-added-tensors argument is in this manuscript.

milne:import:special-point.statement: The special-point theorem is invoked to choose y in the tensor isogeny class I_x with a special-point (hence CM) lift and one quasi-isogeny from C_x preserving crystalline and all prime-to-p tensors. The later proof takes the CM lift over Qbar with the specified reduction place via canonical-model theory.

milne:import:admissible-period-map.statement: For the faithful local Hodge representation, the admissible-locus identity is invoked with ρ^−1(Z_GL)⊂Z_J. The crystalline period map from the framed local Shimura variety has image the J-admissible locus and is étale, so its nonempty fiber over the prescribed classical flag yields a point over a finite extension. The source separately identifies the cohomological period convention, including dual Frobenius descent and the marking.

milne:input:uniformization-condition.statement: The integral-uniformization hypothesis (U_x) is asserted to hold for the adapted global Hodge-type datum by Gleason–Lim–Xu Corollary 6.3, with Pappas–Rapoport Remark 4.10.4 also cited. This is a cited prerequisite of Theorem 4.10.6, not a condition proved by the inventory.

milne:import:integral-uniformization.statement: For global Hodge type, a full connected Bruhat–Tits stabilizer, an adapted integral Hodge embedding, the center's split-rank condition and (U_x), the source invokes a normal formal integral local Shimura variety with a map Θ_x to the completed global model. It is the tensor-compatible open-and-closed part of the Siegel Rapoport–Zink pullback, identifies the tautological framed shtuka and universal p-divisible group, and has the stated local Shimura variety as rigid generic fiber. The source claims the needed theorems include p=2.

milne:import:marked-specialization.statement: The source invokes comparison of the constructed framed point's Breuil–Kisin and Dieudonné specializations and the special-fiber uniformization/isogeny-class map. With identity prime-to-p coordinate, it gives y=i_x(g) and a single abelian quasi-isogeny b:C_x→C_y preserving every designated realization, with the same crystalline marking used by the period map; thus the prescribed flag is b*Fil¹. The displayed cohomological Frobenius is ρ∨(σ(b_x))σ and the lattice is ρ∨(σ(g))D_x_integral.

milne:import:weakly-admissible.statement: For filtered isocrystal data descended to a finite local field, weak admissibility implies admissibility by Colmez–Fontaine. In the applications N=0 gives a crystalline representation, and scalar extension supplies admissibility over the finite extension of K₀. The source expressly restricts inequalities to descended subobjects before applying the theorem.

milne:import:split-weil-reduction.statement: The source attributes the stronger reduction of CM Hodge classes to pullbacks of classes on split-Weil-type varieties to Deligne and André, with Milne's reconstruction cited. Its own lem:cm-reduction instead proves the weaker balanced-signature version directly and does not assume split Hermitian type.

milne:import:markman-weil.statement: For an imaginary quadratic field, the introduction cites algebraicity of Weil classes on abelian fourfolds of Weil type and abelian sixfolds of split Weil type. It explicitly treats these as characteristic-zero antecedents, not as the arbitrary-dimensional input for its rationality proof.

milne:import:good-rational-tate-theory.statement: Rationality for all CM abelian varieties is cited as equivalent to existence of a good theory of rational Tate classes on F-varieties with components products of abelian varieties and projective spaces. Such a theory chooses rational graded algebras whose scalar extensions are the Tate algebras, stable under pullback/pushforward, containing divisors and CM Hodge specializations; it does not assert these classes algebraic.

milne:import:ordinary-cm-case.statement: A CM abelian variety with simple ordinary reduction, and all its powers, is cited as a previous positive rationality case because every divisor on the reduction lifts.

weil:p3ab:split-sixfolds.statement:
\label{p3ab:split-sixfolds}
Let \(E\) be an imaginary quadratic field and let \(A\) be a complex
abelian sixfold with an \(E\)-action.  Suppose a compatible
polarization has hyperbolic rational Hermitian form of signature
\((3,3)\).  Then the rational Hodge conjecture holds in every
codimension on \(A^m\), for every \(m\geq1\).

weil:p3ab:quadratic-five.statement:
\label{p3ab:quadratic-five}
Let \(A\) be a complex abelian variety of dimension at most five
admitting an action of an imaginary quadratic field.  The rational
Hodge conjecture holds in every codimension on \(A^m\), for every
\(m\geq1\).

weil:p3:cm-operations.statement:
\label{p3:cm-operations}
CM supply is preserved by external products, permutations of factors,
cup products, and rational algebraic correspondences.  It is also
preserved by $k$-linear combinations of such correspondences and by
scalar conjugation.  Every rational Hodge class in a CM-supplied
subspace is algebraic.

weil:p3:admissible-operations.statement:
\label{p3:admissible-operations}
Every admissible map is induced on the indicated summands by a
$k$-linear combination of rational algebraic correspondences.
Every pair tensor is algebraic over $k$, and contraction by its
inverse pairing is an algebraic cohomological operation.
If $W$ is admissible, so is $\overline W$, and there is a pair
tensor between $W$ and $\overline W$.

weil:p3:tensor-stabilizer.statement:
\label{p3:tensor-stabilizer}
Inside the symplectic group of $H$, the group
$\operatorname{Hdg}(H)$ is the pointwise stabilizer of all rational
tensors of type $(a,a)$ in $H^{\otimes 2a}$, for all $a\ge0$.

weil:p3:toric-cm-factor.statement:
\label{p3:toric-cm-factor}
Let $A$ be a complex abelian variety and let $H\subset H^1(A,\Q)$ be a
rational Hodge summand.  If $\operatorname{Hdg}(H)$ is a torus, then
$H$ is isomorphic as a rational Hodge structure to $H^1(B,\Q)$ for a
CM isogeny factor $B$ of $A$.

weil:p3:tensor-criterion.statement:
\label{p3:tensor-criterion}
Let $A$ be a complex abelian variety, $H=H^1(A,\Q)$,
$J=\operatorname{Hdg}(H)$, and $R=J^{\mathrm{der}}$.
Suppose the following data exist.

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textnormal{(\alph*)}]
\item A rational Hodge summand $H_0\subset H$ has toric Hodge group.
Choose a decomposition of $H_{0,k}$ into CM embedding lines,
with repeated occurrences distinguished, and call this finite list
$\mathcal E_0$.
\item The complement of $H_{0,k}$ is a direct sum of blocks of
nonzero admissible spaces.  In a symplectic or an orthogonal block,
each space is equipped with an admissible isomorphism to a
representative $V_i$ chosen as an actual summand of that block,
with, respectively, an alternating or a
symmetric pair tensor on itself.  A linear block has
$\dim V_i\ge2$, with $V_i$ again an actual summand, and each space is equipped with an admissible
isomorphism to either $V_i$ or $\overline V_i$, paired with
each other as in Lemma~\ref{p3:admissible-operations}.
The pair identifies $\overline V_i$ with $V_i^*(-1)$ as a
Hodge-graded space and with the dual as a group representation.
\item Under these identifications the image of $R_k$ contains
\[
 P=\prod_{i\in I_{\mathrm{Sp}}}\operatorname{Sp}(V_i)
   \times\prod_{i\in I_{\mathrm{SO}}}\operatorname{SO}(V_i)
   \times\prod_{i\in I_{\mathrm{SL}}}\operatorname{SL}(V_i).
\]
Each factor acts by its standard representation on its own copies,
by the dual representation on the opposite copies of a linear
block, and trivially on every other block and on $H_{0,k}$.
The symplectic and orthogonal forms are the inverse pairings.
\item Let $W_1,\ldots,W_s$ be any list, with arbitrary repetitions,
from
\[
 \{V_i:i\in I_{\mathrm{SO}}\}
 \ \cup\
 \{V_i,\overline V_i:i\in I_{\mathrm{SL}}\}.
\]
Whenever there are $\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_r\in\mathcal E_0$, again
with arbitrary repetitions, such that
\begin{equation}
 \label{p3:eq:determinant-balance}
 \sum_{j=1}^s\epsilon_\gamma(W_j)
 +\sum_{a=1}^r\epsilon_\gamma(\ell_a)=0
 \quad\text{for every }\gamma\in\operatorname{Gal}(k/\Q),
\end{equation}
the line $\bigotimes_{j=1}^sD(W_j)$ is CM-supplied on its
separate tensor slots.  Empty lists are allowed.
\end{enumerate}

Then for every $p\ge0$ every rational balanced tensor in $H^{\otimes 2p}$ is the
class of a rational algebraic cycle on its separate $A$-slots.
The rational Hodge conjecture holds in every codimension of $A^m$
for every $m\ge1$.

Call the data \emph{saturated} if every singleton $D(V_i)$ for
an orthogonal or linear block is CM-supplied, without any balance
condition.  For saturated data and any CM abelian variety $M$,
the induced data on $A\times M$ are saturated.  In particular the
same tensor and Hodge-conjecture conclusions hold for every power of
$A\times M$.

weil:p3:correspondence-transfer.statement:
\label{p3:correspondence-transfer}
Let $\mathscr S$ be a collection of smooth projective varieties such
that the rational Hodge conjecture holds on every finite product of
members of $\mathscr S$.  Let $Y_1,\ldots,Y_v$ be smooth projective
varieties.  Suppose that, for each $i$ and each degree $q$,
$H^q(Y_i,\Q)$ is spanned by images of maps
\[
 \Gamma_*:H^{q-2j}(S,\Q)\longrightarrow H^q(Y_i,\Q),
 \qquad
 \Gamma\in\CH^{\dim S+j}(S\times Y_i)_\Q,\quad S\in\mathscr S.
\]
Then the rational Hodge conjecture holds on every
finite product of the $Y_i$, with arbitrary repetitions and with
any additional members of $\mathscr S$.

The same conclusion holds if the spanning is given over $k$ by
restrictions of maps induced by $k$-linear combinations of
rational algebraic correspondences, provided their images span
the full target degree after scalar extension.

weil:p3sw:weil-plane.statement:
\label{p3sw:weil-plane}
Let \(E\) be an imaginary quadratic field.  Let \(A\) be a complex
abelian sixfold with a unital \(E\)-action and a compatible polarization
whose actual homological Hermitian form \(h_E\) is hyperbolic of signature
\((3,3)\).  Then
\[
 \mathcal W_E(A)\ \subset\
 \operatorname{im}\bigl(\CH^3(A)_\Q
                    \longrightarrow H^6(A,\Q)\bigr).
\]
The assertion holds at every compatible period, including nonsimple
varieties and periods with additional endomorphisms.

weil:p3ab:hyperbolic.statement:
\label{p3ab:hyperbolic}
Let \(E\) be imaginary quadratic.  A nondegenerate \(E\)-Hermitian
form of rank \(2b\) and signature \((b,b)\), \(b\geq1\), is
hyperbolic if and only if
\[
 [\det h]=[(-1)^b].
\]
Every hyperbolic form of this rank is isometric to the sum of \(b\)
planes with matrix
\(\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)\).

weil:p3ab:determinant-supply.statement:
\label{p3ab:determinant-supply}
Let \(A\) be a complex abelian variety with an action of an imaginary
quadratic field \(E\), and let a compatible rational Riemann form
have associated Hermitian form of signature \((p,q)\).
Put \(n=\dim A=p+q\).  Both lines
\[
 D\bigl(H^1(A,k)_\sigma\bigr),\qquad
 D\bigl(H^1(A,k)_{\bar\sigma}\bigr)
\]
are CM-supplied in either of the following cases:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \(n=6\), \((p,q)=(3,3)\), and the form is hyperbolic;
\item \(n<6\) and \(p,q\leq3\).
\end{enumerate}
The second assertion permits every compatible rational Riemann form.
Both assertions hold at every period.

weil:p3ab:albert-columns.statement:
\label{p3ab:albert-columns}
In Types I--III let \(F=Z(D)\) be totally real of degree \(f\).
In Type IV let the CM center \(K=Z(D)\) have degree \(2f\), and
write \([D:K]=b^2\).  The columns in
\eqref{p3ab:eq:columns} have the following data:
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}
 \text{Albert type}&\text{necessary divisibility}&\dim_k W&
       \text{pair tensor}\\ \hline
 \mathrm I& f\mid g&2g/f&\text{alternating on }W\\
 \mathrm{II}&2f\mid g&g/f&\text{alternating on }W\\
 \mathrm{III}&2f\mid g&g/f&\text{symmetric on }W\\
 \mathrm{IV}&fb^2\mid g&g/(fb)&\text{between opposite columns}.
\end{array}
\]
The listed tensors are pair tensors in the sense of
Section~\ref{p3:sec:tensors}, and all copy identifications are
admissible.  In Type IV the opposite column is the dual
\(R_B\)-module.

weil:p3ab:minuscule.statement:
\label{p3ab:minuscule}
In the irreducible tensor decomposition of a column \(W_\tau\) for
the simple ideals of \(\operatorname{Lie}(R_B)_k\), every nontrivial
simple factor representation is minuscule.

weil:p3ab:small-projections.statement:
\label{p3ab:small-projections}
An alternating self-paired column of dimension \(2,4\), or \(6\)
has the full symplectic derived image.  A symmetric self-paired
column cannot have dimension two; in dimensions four and six its
derived image is, respectively, the full \(\operatorname{SO}_4\)
and \(\operatorname{SO}_6\).

If \(D=K\) is an imaginary quadratic field, \(B\) is non-CM, and
\(\dim_K H_B\leq6\), then the derived image on either embedding
column is the full special linear group, with dual action on the
opposite column.

weil:p3ab:small-columns.statement:
\label{p3ab:small-columns}
Let \(A\) have an imaginary-quadratic \(E\)-action and
\(\dim A\leq6\).  Write \(A\sim\prod_B B^{r_B}\) with pairwise
nonisogenous simple factors, and discard the CM factors.  Put
\(g=\dim B\).  After identifying matrix copies, the remaining
columns have the following possibilities.
\begin{enumerate}
\item In Types I and II they have full symplectic derived images
and dimensions \(2,4,6\).
\item In Type III, \(g=4\) or \(6\), the center is \(\Q\), and
\(r_B=1\).  The unique column has full
\(\operatorname{SO}_g\) image.  Each eigenspace of the given
\(E\)-action is one copy of this column and has equal Hodge
multiplicities \(g/2,g/2\).
\item In Type IV, \(D=K\) is a CM field.  If \(E\) admits no
\(\Q\)-embedding into \(K\), then \(K\) is imaginary quadratic,
\(g=3\), and \(r_B=2\); the \(K\)-columns have the full
\(\operatorname{SL}_3\) and dual images.

If \(E\) admits a \(\Q\)-embedding into \(K\), put
\([K:\Q]=2f\) and \(a=g/f\).  The possibilities are
\[
 f=1,\quad 3\leq a=g\leq6;
 \qquad (f,a,g)=(2,2,4),(2,3,6),(3,2,6).
\]
Every column has the full \(\operatorname{SL}_a\) image,
paired with the dual at the opposite embedding.  In the cases
with \(a=2\), some embedding pairs are mixed and some are pure.
\end{enumerate}
All these are projections of the actual derived Hodge group of \(A\).

weil:p3ab:independence.statement:
\label{p3ab:independence}
In Lemma~\ref{p3ab:small-columns}, the listed symplectic,
orthogonal, and special linear derived images are independent,
after identifying matrix copies and pairing opposite CM embeddings.
In other words, they satisfy assumption \textnormal{(c)} of
Theorem~\ref{p3:tensor-criterion}.

weil:p3sw:invariant-orbit-ext.statement: {"hypotheses": ["Gamma is a finite subgroup of the same Jacobian X of order n.", "Z is a disjoint union of n Abel curves permuted transitively by Gamma, and I_Z has its canonical linearization."], "assertions": ["As Gamma-representations, Ext\u00b9_X(I_Z,I_Z) is isomorphic to H\u00b9(X,O_X) direct_sum direct_sum_{j=1}^n H^0(X,T_X).", "The first summand is trivial; the second has the regular permutation action on components and identity action on each translation space.", "dim_C Ext\u00b9_X(I_Z,I_Z)^Gamma=6, dim_C Ext\u00b2_X(I_Z,I_Z)^Gamma=6, and Hom_X(I_Z,I_Z)^Gamma=C."]}

weil:p3sw:invariant-ext.statement: {"hypotheses": ["I_script=I_Sigma external_tensor I_A is the seed source on X\u00b2 with its canonical G_src=G_1 times G_2 linearization."], "assertions": ["The invariant subspace of the full derived group Ext\u00b2_{X\u00b2}(I_script,I_script) has dimension 6+36+6=48."]}

weil:p3sw:invariant-one-factor-rank.statement: {"context": "For a perfect object Q, c_Q^k:HT^k(X)->HOmega_{-k}(X) is contraction with the raw first-jet Hodge character in the fixed left-interior convention. For either seed orbit ideal, ch_H(I_Z)=f_n=1-(n/2)theta_H\u00b2+(n/3)theta_H\u00b3.", "assertions": ["For either orbit ideal I_Z, c_{I_Z}\u00b9 is injective of rank six, and c_{I_Z}\u00b2 is surjective of rank six."]}

weil:p3sw:invariant-product-rank.statement: {"hypotheses": ["I_script=I_Sigma external_tensor I_A is the seed source with the preceding raw Hodge-character and contraction conventions."], "assertions": ["c_{I_script}\u00b2:HT\u00b2(X\u00b2)->HOmega_{-2}(X\u00b2) has rank 48."]}

weil:p3sw:invariant-injectivity.statement: {"context": "o_Q=ob_Q and sigma_Q are the full perfect-trace maps. I_script has its canonical G_src action; G=tildePhi(I_script)[-3] has the coherently conjugated line-translation action of Gbar on M.", "assertions": ["im(o_I)=Ext\u00b2_{X\u00b2}(I,I)^{G_src}, ker(o_I)=ker(c_I\u00b2), and sigma_I is injective on that full invariant group.", "im(o_G)=Ext\u00b2_M(G,G)^{Gbar}, ker(o_G)=ker(c_G\u00b2), and sigma_G is injective on that full invariant group."]}

weil:p3sw:fourier-matrix.statement: {"context": "ell_X=6=2g_X, g_X=3; e_i is an oriented basis of L=H\u00b9(X,Q) with integral e_1...e_6=1, f_i the dual basis of U=H\u00b9(Xhat,Q), p=sum e_i wedge f_i, and epsilon_{I,J} is the ordered shuffle sign. F_-(alpha)=(-1)^{g_X}(pi_Xhat)_*(exp(-p)pi_X^*alpha).", "assertions": ["For every subset P of {1,...,ell_X}, with k=|P|, F_-(e_P)=(-1)^{k(k+3)/2} epsilon_{P,P^c} f_{P^c}.", "F_- is a rational parity-preserving isomorphism."]}

weil:p3sw:spin-identity.statement: {"context": "V=L direct_sum U has split symmetric Q with Q(e_i,f_j)=delta_ij. Clifford relation is vw+wv=Q(v,w). Spin acts by m_g on S=Lambda L and by rho(g) on V. rho'_g=phi'(m_g tensor m_g)(phi')^{-1}, with phi' the fixed Fourier/shear/reversal map.", "assertions": ["For every algebraic spin element g, rho'_g=exp(p/2) Lambda rho(g) exp(-p/2)=exp((p-Lambda\u00b2 rho(g)p)/2) Lambda rho(g), as an exact equality of rational algebraic representations; exponentials act by exterior multiplication.", "[rho'_g(1)]_0=1 and [rho'_g(1)]_2=(p-Lambda\u00b2 rho(g)p)/2."], "limitations": "The quantifier is not restricted to spin elements preserving the initial Hodge structure or realized by derived autoequivalences."}

weil:p3sw:polarized-seed.statement: {"context": "K=Q(u), u\u00b2=-d, d>=3; M=X times Xhat is the actual seed sixfold, a=-lambda, vartheta(y)=iota_y Theta, lambda_+=exp(uTheta), lambda_-=exp(-uTheta). J fixes the rational spinor plane pointwise; Ltilde_K preserves the two individual spinor lines in order.", "assertions": ["eta(u)(x,N)=(a^{-1}(N),[-d]a(x))=(-lambda^{-1}(N),[d]lambda(x)) defines a unital K-action on M.", "L_M=pr_X^*H^d tensor pr_Xhat^*(a^{-1})^*H is ample; its normalized class theta_M is fixed by the vector images of J and Ltilde_K.", "The action is of Weil type (3,3), compatible with this polarization, and its actual homological second-linear Hermitian form is hyperbolic.", "On cohomology f=eta(u)^* sends (w,y) to (d vartheta y,-vartheta^{-1}w), and f\u00b2=-d.", "W_+=Ann(lambda_+)={(-u vartheta y,y):y in U_K} has eigenvalue +u, and W_-=Ann(lambda_-)={(u vartheta y,y):y in U_K} has eigenvalue -u."]}

weil:p3sw:ordered-stabilizer.statement: {"context": "W=W_+ has K-dimension six, and V_K=W direct_sum W* via Q. Identify the Clifford module with Lambda W.", "assertions": ["Ltilde_K={(g,t) in GL(W) times G_m:t\u00b2=det g}, acting by m(g,t)=t^{-1}Lambda g; J_K={(g,1):g in SL(W)}.", "The characters on lambda_+,lambda_- are respectively t,t^{-1}.", "For every 0<=j<=6, H^{2j}(M,Q)^J=Q theta_M^j if j!=3, and H^6(M,Q)^J=Q theta_M\u00b3 direct_sum W_K(M). All odd cohomological invariants vanish.", "The ordered line stabilizer fixes every theta_M^j and acts on the two scalar Weil lines by t\u00b2,t^{-2}."], "limitations": "This is an algebraic-group statement, not an assertion that every K-rational determinant has a square root in K. The element (1,-1) fixes the lines but is not in the pointwise stabilizer."}

weil:p3sw:exceptional-character.statement: {"context": "E is the actual seed sheaf of rank r=8d and kappa_M=exp(-c_{1,B}(E)/r)ch_B(E).", "assertions": ["kappa_M is a rational, J-invariant, even class.", "Its degree-six component is (kappa_M)_3=a_M theta_M\u00b3+w_M with a_M in Q and 0!=w_M in the rational Weil plane W_K(M)."]}

weil:p3sw:hodge-circle.statement: {"hypotheses": ["Keep the rational homology of the seed M, its action eta, and the Riemann form of L_M fixed."], "assertions": ["At every compatible marked complex structure of Weil type (3,3), every component (kappa_M)_j has Hodge type (j,j)."]}

weil:p3sw:descent-duality.statement: {"context": "E=RHom_M(G,O_M)[-1] is the actual seed sheaf, with the dual coherent inverse-line translation action. Use raw a=-At_BF and the full perfect-trace semiregularity map.", "assertions": ["Even transpose induces an isomorphism d_2:Ext\u00b2_M(G,G)^{Gbar}->Ext\u00b2_M(E,E)^{Gbar}.", "For every j>=0, sigma_{E,j}(d_2v)=(-1)^{j+1}sigma_{G,j}(v).", "Injectivity of sigma_G on the full invariant Ext\u00b2 therefore implies injectivity of sigma_E on the full invariant Ext\u00b2."]}

weil:p3sw:twisted-descent.statement: {"context": "q:M->Y_0=M/Gbar is the finite-etale translation isogeny; E has rank r=8d and coherent line-twisted action.", "assertions": ["There exist alpha in H\u00b2(Y_0,mu_r), a coherent alpha-twisted sheaf B of rank r with det B isomorphic to O_{Y_0}, and an invertible q^*alpha-twisted sheaf L on M, such that q^*B isomorphic to E tensor L.", "For every integer i, on the mu_r-gerbe Yfrak_0 of alpha, Ext^i(B,B) isomorphic to Ext^i_M(E,E)^{Gbar}, and the same holds for the trace-free kernels Ext^i_0.", "For lambda_H=a_{det E}/r=tr(a_E)/r, the degree-two comparison phi satisfies q^*sigma_B(v)=exp(-lambda_H)sigma_E(phi(v)), on full Ext and its trace-free summand.", "Thus full invariant semiregularity of E makes B semiregular; by p3sw:descent-duality, full invariant injectivity for G suffices."], "associated_postproof_assertion": "Lines 6088-6110 give q^*ch_H(B)=exp(-lambda_H)ch_H(E) and q^*ch_B(B)=exp(-c_1^B(det E)/r)ch_B(E).
